Week 8: your app, version 1

Midterm deliverable: a working app on top of your aggregator, shown to the class, with a 5-minute explanation of how you know its numbers are right. This notebook is a starter app. It has the four parts every app in this course needs:
  1. Filters so a reader can narrow the data down.
  2. A chart of the numbers.
  3. A table with the actual rows behind the chart.
  4. A "Where these numbers came from" panel that is always on screen: the sources, the reporting periods, and how many hospitals were left out of the chart and why.
Use it as it is with the course's default layer, or upload your own week-3 export. Then change it, with your AI tool's help, until it answers your question.

1. Choose your layer

Option A, the course default layer (nothing to do): one row per hospital, with one CMS measure and one county health measure. You can swap the two measures here: Option B, your own layer: upload the CSV you exported in week 3. It should have one row per hospital. If you upload a file, the app uses it instead of the default.

3. Run it as an app and share it

On your own computer. Open a terminal in the folder that holds this file and run 
marimo run week08_app_starter.py
marimo opens the notebook in your browser as an app: code hidden, controls working. marimo edit week08_app_starter.py reopens it for editing. In molab (marimo's free hosted service, https://molab.marimo.io/notebooks). Save a copy to your own workspace first (Save a copy, or Fork on the preview page). Then click Share: Copy Notebook URL gives viewers a preview they can run or copy, and Copy App URL shares it as a data app with the code hidden. If the menus look different from that description, trust what you see, and check https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/. Before you share: open your link in a private browser window to check a classmate can open it, and check the app only uses public, aggregate data.

4. Make it yours: Ask your AI

Paste one of these into the AI tool you use, together with the code of the cell you want changed (in molab or marimo edit, show the code of a cell with its "show code" toggle).
"This is a marimo notebook cell that draws an Altair chart from a pandas DataFrame called charted. Change it to a bar chart of the median of cms_score by state, one bar per state, sorted high to low. Keep the row count in the title. Don't turn missing values into zero." "Add a marimo dropdown that filters layer by overall_rating. Put it next to the state filter. Show the number of rows before and after the filter." "My week-3 export has these columns: [paste the column names]. Which of them should the 'Where these numbers came from' panel list as reporting periods, and why?"
After every change, check two things yourself: the row counts in the panel still add up, and one number in the table still matches the source file.

Before you submit

Deliverable: a working app link a classmate can open, and a 5-minute explanation in class of how you know its numbers are right. The one check: pick one hospital in your table and find its number in the original source file (the source page is in the panel). Say in your explanation which hospital you checked.
